sentences.text: Asif Manzoor Shaikh vs The State Of Maharashtra on 5
December, 2025

In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. Of 2025
 (@ Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No.11751/2025)
 Asif Manzoor Shaikh ...Appellant(S)
 Versus
 The State Of Maharashtra & Anr. .Respondent(S)
O R D E R Leave granted.

This appeal challenges the judgment and order dated 21.07.2025 passed by the Bombay High Court,
in Bail Application No. 2437 of 2025.
The appellant Asif Manzoor Shaikh has been facing trial in connection with a crime registered pursuant to FIR No. 50 of 2023 dated 19.01.2023 lodged with Police Station Shanti Nagar, District Thane City in respect of offences punishable under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468 and 471 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 [in short, IPC]
The application seeking regular bail having been rejected by the High Court vide impugned order dated 21.07.2025, the appellant has preferred the instant appeal.
This Court, vide its order dated 11.08.2025, issued notice in the instant matter.
We have heard learned senior counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the respondent(s) and perused the material on record.
Learned senior counsel for the appellant submitted that the allegations as against the appellant herein are not true at all; that for a period of nine months he has been in jail.
The charges against the appellant are triable by the learned Magistrate.

In the circumstances, the relief of bail may be Asif Manzoor Shaikh vs The State Of Maharashtra on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163257729/
1 granted to the appellant herein by setting aside the impugned order.

sentences.text: Learned senior counsel also submitted that the appellant would make all efforts to ensure that the building put up by him is ultimately regularized and there would be no constraints on the purchasers of the flats such as respondent No.2 herein.
Therefore, the appeal may be allowed.
Learned senior counsel for the appellant further submitted that in compliance of the interim order of this Court, the appellant surrendered on 01/03.12.2025.

Per contra, learned counsel for the first respondent  State as well as the learned counsel for the second respondent-complainant with reference to their counter affidavits submitted that there is no merit in this appeal; that the appellant has no intention to secure the regularisation of the building; that any relief granted to the appellant herein would only result in frustration of the trial.
He, therefore submitted that appeal may be dismissed.
Considering the facts on record, in our view, the case for regular bail is made out.

We, therefore, allow this appeal and direct as under:
The appellant Asif Manzoor Shaikh shall be produced before the concerned trial Court as early as possible and the trial Court shall release him on bail, subject to such conditions as it may deem appropriate to impose to ensure his presence in the proceedings arising out of FIR No. 50 of 2023 mentioned above.
It is directed that the appellant shall extend complete cooperation in the trial of the instant case.
The appellant shall not misuse his liberty in any manner.
Any infraction of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail granted to the appellant.
With these observations, the appeal is allowed.

J. [B.V. NAGARATHNA] .J.
[K.V. VISWANATHAN]
